overclaims: No company, regulator or analyst publishes the dollar value of uninstalled or unpowered NVIDIA hardware, so no public measure exists to test this range against.
This confirms there is no direct public measure of idle chips.
Shows one large buyer holding NVIDIA racks before power is ready, on the order of billions per month.
This is far smaller than the claimed range and covers one company only.
checks.note: The criteria and e3 explanation turn a gap in the packet into a universal claim that no public measure exists. Epoch's uncertainty does not establish that. The e2 explanation treats projected deliveries as observed holdings and compares a monthly flow with an accumulated stock. The rationale's qualifications do not fix these statements elsewhere.

overclaims: Confirms that one named firm holds billions of NVIDIA hardware ahead of power in the target period.
checks.note: The e1 explanation converts projected rack deliveries into confirmed holdings worth billions during the target period. The report supports staging hardware before deployment, but does not establish the realized dollar value held then. The rationale and limitations correctly preserve this distinction; the evidence explanation must do so too.
